title: A Geometric Journey Through the Aharonov--Bohm Effect: Tonomura's Toroid, Pseudoscalar Phase, and Quantum Holonomy in Clifford Algebra
abstract: The magnetic Aharonov--Bohm (AB) effect is often introduced through the idealised infinite solenoid and a complex scalar phase. We give a geometric-algebra formulation based on the compact toroidal magnets shielded by a superconductor employed in the electron-holography experiments of Tonomura and collaborators. Working in the real Euclidean Clifford algebra $ \mathrm{Cl}(3,0)$, we distinguish the unit volume pseudoscalar $I$ (grade 3), coordinate angles (scalars, grade 0), tangent vectors (grade 1), and directed surface bivectors (grade 2). The magnetic field is represented by the dual bivector $\mathcal{B}= I \mathbf B$, while the electromagnetic $U(1)$ phase is represented by the central unit multivector $e^{I\alpha}$ generated by the pseudoscalar $I$, rather than by a spatial rotor with a bivector generator. We establish the linked toroidal geometry, formulate magnetic flux and Stokes' theorem intrinsically in geometric algebra, and derive the holonomy element $U_\Gamma=\exp(Iq\Phi_B/\hbar)$ from $U(1)$ gauge covariance, with every sign fixed explicitly. We then express superconducting fluxoid quantization in the same notation and obtain the binary electron holonomy $U_\Gamma = (-1)^N$ in the ideal limit where the linked magnetic flux equals $N h/(2e)$. Finally, a short conditional-state description of the quantum source and field shows how a backreaction can introduce an additional phase and reduce interference visibility. The conditional-state overlap is represented by a central scalar--pseudoscalar element; preservation of the fluxoid sector alone does not guarantee unit coherence.

summaries.en: The paper reformulates the magnetic Aharonov–Bohm effect in real Euclidean Clifford algebra Cl(3,0) using Tonomura's superconducting toroidal magnets, representing the magnetic field by a dual bivector and the U(1) phase by the central pseudoscalar-generated unit multivector to derive the holonomy U_Γ = exp(IqΦ_B/ℏ) with explicit signs, express fluxoid quantization and the binary electron holonomy (-1)^N, and show via a conditional-state description that backreaction can add a phase and reduce interference visibility.

title: Dynamics and pseudospectra around quantum exceptional points
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) are a hallmark of non-Hermitian physics, giving rise to extreme sensitivity and enhanced dynamic response. Such unique spectral singularities have been extensively studied in classical photonics, both at theoretical and experimental levels, where the relevant observables are evident. That is not necessarily the case in the quantum regime, where this kind of behavior around EPs, to a large extent, remains elusive. In fact, the interplay between dissipation and quantum fluctuations makes the complete Lindbladian evolution quite different from effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian descriptions. In this context, we investigate the signatures of the Liouvillian EPs on spectral and dynamic response by considering properly normalized long-time averages and imbalances. Even though our approach is generic, we focus on two paradigmatic models-a lossy Bose-Hubbard lattice and a dissipative two-spin system, where we investigate the role of quantum jumps and interactions in the Liouvillian spectrum, in terms of complex and structured pseudospectra. Our results demonstrate how non-Hermitian phenomena emerge in realistic quantum lattices, providing a bridge between classical EP physics and experimentally accessible open quantum systems.

summaries.en: This paper investigates the signatures of Liouvillian exceptional points on spectral and dynamic response in open quantum systems, using properly normalized long-time averages and imbalances to show how quantum jumps and interactions shape complex pseudospectra in a lossy Bose-Hubbard lattice and a dissipative two-spin system.
summaries.zh: 本文通过采用适当归一化的长期平均和不平衡量，研究了开放量子系统中Liouvillian例外点对光谱和动力学响应的特征，并在有损耗的Bose-Hubbard晶格和耗散双自旋系统中展示了量子跳跃和相互作用如何塑造复杂的伪谱。

title: Resonance-engineered single-photon routing in an asymmetric Jaynes-Cummings cavity-waveguide system
abstract: We investigate single-photon scattering and routing in an asymmetric cavity-waveguide quantum electrodynamics system consisting of a Jaynes-Cummings cavity-emitter subsystem coupled to two one-dimensional waveguides. Using a real-space scattering approach, we derive an exact three-channel scattering matrix and analytical expressions for the channel-resolved scattering amplitudes. The scattering response is governed by the interplay of asymmetric cavity-waveguide coupling, atom-cavity detuning, coherent preparation of a single-photon superposition across multiple input channels, and intrinsic dissipation. Coupling asymmetry controls the relative weights of the cavity-mediated scattering pathways, whereas atom-cavity detuning modifies their spectral response. Coherent multichannel input states provide an additional phase-sensitive control of the output probabilities through interference. In particular, we identify an analytical condition, $J_2=2J_1$ and $\alpha_1=-\alpha_2$, under which the probability in the second output channel becomes independent of photon energy; for an equal-weight normalized input, this probability is 1/2. We further show how cavity and atomic dissipation reduce the probability remaining in the guided channels. These results provide a framework for resonance-engineered single-photon routing in asymmetric Jaynes-Cummings cavity-waveguide systems.

summaries.en: The paper derives an exact three-channel scattering matrix for single-photon scattering in an asymmetric Jaynes-Cummings cavity-waveguide system and shows that cavity-waveguide coupling asymmetry, atom-cavity detuning, coherent multichannel input superpositions, and dissipation jointly control photon routing, with a specific resonance condition making the second-channel output probability energy-independent and equal to 1/2 for an equal-weight input.

title: A Phase-Balanced Differential Rydberg-Atom Quantum Receiver for Weak GNSS Signal Detection
abstract: This paper proposes a phase-balanced differential Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (DRAQR) for weak-signal recovery, using local-oscillator phase control to reinforce differential signal responses and a shared squeezed-reservoir model to correlate inter-cell quantum projection noise (QPN) and photon shot noise (PSN). An analytical model incorporating QPN, PSN, intrinsic thermal noise (ITN), and inter-cell correlations quantifies signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain, outage-constrained minimum detectable power, and bit-error rate (BER) for square $M$-QAM. For the evaluated settings, SNR gain reaches approximately $10$~dB as PSN correlation approaches unity, with BER decreasing as correlation increases. Under Rician fading, at a $0$-dB threshold SNR and maximum outage probability of $0.1$, the minimum detectable power decreases from $-146.95$~dBm at $K=1.155$ to $-159.98$~dBm at $K=2.4$. Analytical results are validated against Monte-Carlo simulations over $150{,}000$ data runs per point for receiver-performance plots.

summaries.en: The paper proposes a phase-balanced differential Rydberg-atom quantum receiver that exploits local-oscillator phase control and a shared squeezed-reservoir model to correlate quantum projection noise and photon shot noise, analytically quantifying up to ~10 dB SNR gain and showing that under Rician fading the outage-constrained minimum detectable power improves from -146.

title: Shaping Frequency-Bin Biphoton Correlations via Programmable Optical Frequency Combs
abstract: Programmable shaping of photon-pair spectral correlations is important for frequency-bin quantum information processing. However, achieving this control remains challenging in nonlinear optical systems without reliable forward models. Here, we demonstrate model-free, hardware-in-the-loop shaping of the measured joint spectral intensity of a cascaded photon-pair source driven by a programmable optical frequency comb. A blockwise simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation controller optimizes up to 22 pump, signal, and idler parameters. Each iteration requires only two accepted hardware evaluations, independent of the parameter count. The controller converges to diverse target patterns on 3$\times$3, 4$\times$4, and 5$\times$5 frequency-bin grids. The optimized distributions achieve Pearson correlations between 0.66 and 0.98 and classical overlap fidelities between 0.32 and 0.62. Cross-target similarity analysis confirms that the optimized patterns remain target-specific. Source characterization yields a maximum coincidence-to-accidental ratio of approximately 585. Accuracy is limited by pump-phase transfer, parasitic nonlinear background, waveshaper constraints, amplitude-only filtering, and measurement noise. Joint spectral intensity contains no spectral-phase information. Therefore, the results demonstrate control of measured frequency-bin populations and correlations, not complete reconstruction of the two-photon state. Phase-sensitive characterization is required to verify inter-bin coherence and quantify the entanglement dimensionality of the output state. Our results establish direct measurement feedback as a practical approach to reconfigurable frequency-bin correlation engineering when an accurate end-to-end model is unavailable.

title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
abstract: We propose a synthetic temporal-mode converter (STC) that combines programmable waveform matching with denser time multiplexing for heterogeneous quantum interconnects. Programmable couplers and optical delays reshape known single-photon temporal waveforms through coherent interference between time bins. Conversion to a common single-bin mode concentrates amplitudes from $N$ bins in $\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ mixing stages, simultaneously improving temporal indistinguishability and freeing channel time. Simulations yield mode overlaps above 99.9\% for exponential and Gaussian inputs. For $N=256$ and $0.5\,\mathrm{dB}$ loss per stage, STC gives a 45.6-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate than temporal gating at equal mode overlap for two exponential inputs. Relative to long pulses, the shortened temporal matched mode can support an approximately 41-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate when the available time-multiplexing capacity is fully utilized.

title: Differentiable Digital Twins for Optimization, Calibration, and Characterization of Neutral-Atom- and Ion-based Quantum Computers
abstract: Quantum technologies based on individually controlled atoms are among the most promising platforms for scalable quantum computing, owing to their favorable coherence properties and controllability. Nonetheless, achieving reliable and high-fidelity gate operations remains challenging due to the sensitivity of these systems to noise and hardware imperfections. In this work, we introduce a comprehensive software toolset designed to model atomic quantum systems with high precision and simulate qubit gate dynamics. By integrating quantum optimal control and benchmarking techniques with automatic differentiation for efficient and accurate gradient-based optimization, the toolset enables significant improvements in gate performance. We demonstrate its capabilities through detailed case studies involving both neutral atoms and trapped ions, highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing quantum gate fidelities, and providing valuable insights for experimental implementation.

summaries.en: The authors introduce a differentiable software toolset that models neutral-atom and trapped-ion quantum systems and combines quantum optimal control and benchmarking with automatic differentiation to optimize, calibrate, and characterize gate operations, demonstrating improved gate fidelities in case studies for both platforms.

title: 13,000-Fold Frequency Down Conversion From 280 MHz to 21 kHz Using Mechanical Frequency Combs
abstract: Optical frequency combs bridge the microwave and terahertz regimes by down-converting terahertz optical energy into microwave signals. A photodetector converts the comb's equally spaced lines, generated through optical nonlinearities, into a low-frequency tone at their spacing. Here, we present the first mechanical version of this process, using mechanical frequency combs to downconvert energy over 4 orders of magnitude, from the MHz to kHz regime. Thin-film lithium niobate (LN) is used to design an acoustic resonator with a wide range of mode frequencies. We achieve phononic comb excitation from 250 MHz to 900 MHz and compare the electrical and laser Doppler vibrometer (LDV) measurements at 277 MHz. We then show the low-frequency spectrum of the devices, highlighting mechanical motion at the comb's spacing and demonstrating energy transfer from 277 MHz to 21 kHz.

summaries.en: Researchers demonstrate the first mechanical frequency comb in thin-film lithium niobate, using it to down-convert phononic comb signals from 277 MHz to 21 kHz, achieving roughly 13,000-fold frequency reduction over four orders of magnitude.
summaries.zh: 研究人员在薄膜铌酸锂中实现了首个机械频率梳，利用其将277 MHz的声子梳信号下变频至21 kHz，实现了约13000倍、跨越四个数量级的频率降低。

title: Energy-Aware Vertically Layered Pinching-Antenna System Design with Probabilistic LoS Availability
abstract: This paper investigates a vertically layered pinching antenna (PA) system, in which dielectric waveguides deployed at different heights provide additional vertical spatial degrees of freedom for line-of-sight (LoS)-favorable PA placement. We consider a practical energy model that captures in-waveguide attenuation, base station-to-feed-point optical-fiber loss, and PA repositioning energy, along with a statistical LoS-availability model that depends on elevation and distance. We then jointly optimize the transmit beamforming, PA positions, time allocation, and transmission rates to maximize the expected successfully delivered frame-effective sum rate under per-user outage and quality-of-service constraints. To avoid enumerating the exponentially many LoS states, we derive a certified conditional-moment outage envelope for outage-guaranteed rate selection and a differentiable safe approximation of the chance constraints to facilitate tractable optimization. Building on these results, a block coordinate descent algorithm with a penalty-aided majorization-minimization procedure attains a high-quality suboptimal solution. Simulation results confirm the gains of vertical layering and reveal a fundamental energy-LoS tradeoff: LoS-favorable PA placement generally enhances both performance and reliability, although it incurs higher attenuation, path loss, and energy costs.

summaries.en: This paper jointly optimizes transmit beamforming, pinching-antenna positions, time allocation, and transmission rates to maximize the expected frame-effective sum rate in a vertically layered pinching-antenna system under an energy model and probabilistic LoS availability, using a certified conditional-moment outage envelope and a differentiable safe approximation of the chance constraints within a block coordinate descent algorithm.
summaries.zh: 本文针对垂直分层夹持天线系统，在考虑波导内衰减、光纤损耗和天线重定位能耗的能量模型以及依赖仰角与距离的概率性视距可用性模型下，通过联合优化发射波束成形、夹持天线位置、时间分配和传输速率来最大化期望帧有效和速率，并采用经认证的条件矩中断包络与机会约束的可微安全近似，在块坐标下降算法中求得高质量次优解。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、垂直方向に層状化したピンチングアンテナシステムにおいて、導波路内減衰・光ファイバ損失・アンテナ再配置エネルギーを考慮したエネルギー模型と仰角および距離に依存する確率的LoS可用性モデルの下で、送信ビームフォーミング・ピンチングアンテナ位置・時間割当・伝送レートを共同最適化して期待フレーム有効和レートを最大化し、認証済み条件付きモーメント outage エンベロープとチャンス制約の微分可能な安全近似を用いたブロック座標降下法により高品質な準最適解を得る。

title: An Ultra-Low-Noise Tunable TIA in 45nm Silicon Photonics for Electro-Optical Ultrasound Data Acquisition
abstract: This paper presents the design and experimental characterization of a 32-channel, WDM-compatible electronic-photonic receiver array fabricated in the GlobalFoundries 45nm monolithic silicon photonics process. Optimized for miniaturized, millimeter-scale electro-optical ultrasound data acquisition probes for broadband photo-acoustic imaging (PAI), the chip utilizes integrated micro-ring resonator (MRR) demultiplexers and photodiode (PD) arrays to decode multi-wavelength acoustic signals outside the body. This work focuses specifically on the comprehensive characterization of the receiver front-end, evaluating both the optical WDM filter bank and the transimpedance amplifier (TIA) performance. Monolithic co-integration minimizes critical photodiode-to-TIA interface parasitics. The TIA incorporates a DC-offset cancellation loop that compensates for photodiode-induced offset currents while providing tunable low-frequency cutoff control over a range of 30 kHz to 1.5 MHz. This tunability enables effective suppression of flicker noise and improves overall signal integrity. The front-end achieves the peak transimpedance gain of 144 dB$\Omega$ while maintaining an ultra-low input-referred noise current density of $1\text{ pA}/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$, demonstrating a highly scalable architecture for high-sensitivity intravascular and endobronchial imaging.

summaries.en: This paper presents a 32-channel WDM-compatible electronic-photonic receiver array in a 45nm monolithic silicon photonics process featuring micro-ring demultiplexers and photodiodes, with a transimpedance amplifier achieving 144 dBΩ gain and 1 pA/√Hz input-referred noise density and a tunable 30 kHz to 1.
summaries.zh: 本文介绍了一种采用45纳米单片硅光子工艺制造的32通道、兼容波分复用的电子-光子接收器阵列，其集成微环解复用器和光电二极管，跨阻放大器实现144 dBΩ峰值增益和1 pA/√Hz的超低输入参考噪声电流密度，并具有30 kHz至1.
summaries.ja: 本論文は、45nmモノリシックシリコンフォトニクスプロセスで作製された32チャネルのWDM対応電子-フォトニック受信アレイを提示し、マイクロリングデマルチプレクサとフォトダイオードを備え、トランスインピーダンスアンプが144 dBΩのピーク利得と1 pA/√Hzの超低入力換算ノイズ電流密度、および30 kHzから1.
